short: Seventy-four days that toppled a junta and secured a prime minister.
full:
Argentina's military junta, led by General Leopoldo Galtieri, invaded the Falkland Islands on 2 April 1982, seizing a British overseas territory that Argentina claims as the Malvinas. Britain assembled a naval task force within days and sent it 8,000 miles south. The sinking of the cruiser General Belgrano on 2 May and the loss of HMS Sheffield two days later set the character of a war fought largely at sea and in the air, in which Argentine aircraft sank six British ships.

Troops landed at San Carlos Water on 21 May and fought across East Falkland at Goose Green, Mount Longdon, Two Sisters and Tumbledown. Argentine forces surrendered at Stanley on 14 June, seventy-four days after the invasion. The dead numbered 649 Argentine servicemen, 255 British and three islanders. Defeat destroyed the junta and brought civilian rule back to Argentina in 1983; victory helped return Margaret Thatcher's government with a large majority the same year. Sabaton's "Back in Control", from Attero Dominatus (2006), is about the campaign.
